headline: Keys giving administrator access to Fugaku's servers were taken; Japan asked other supercomputer operators to check their systems.
summary: 4 new sources (1 Tier 1: the education minister's Nov 17 press conference transcript; 3 Tier 2: Nikkei, Kyodo via Sankei, BleepingComputer). Added c014 (administrator-access keys taken, Confirmed), c015 (investigative committee with outside experts, Confirmed), c016 (ministry asked other supercomputer operators to check their systems, Confirmed on two independent outlets). Noted RIKEN's plan to fix vulnerabilities in the exploited software on c002 and q002. Timeline rows t008 to t010. Staleness check done: head, known, not_known and who_is_affected reviewed; checked-not-found note refreshed. Privacy check done: no individuals named.

headline: RIKEN says an outsider entered Fugaku through its public status dashboard and took 430 private keys; the machine is offline.
summary: First draft. 4 sources (2 Tier 1), 13 claims (9 Confirmed, 1 Reported, 3 Not established), 6 questions. RIKEN's two notices confirm the break-in, the stolen keys and the user counts. The attacker and any use of the keys elsewhere are not established. Shutdown time follows RIKEN (Nov 14, 4:30 AM Japan time). Privacy check done: no individuals named, no contact details.
